I implemented intermediate-layer prediction and switchable dropout for uncertainty estimation across four source files (no test files touched).

**`deepchem/models/layers.py`** — Added the `SwitchedDropout(tf.keras.layers.Layer)` class. It takes a `rate` in its constructor and `call([tensor, switch])` two inputs: it computes `rate = self.rate * tf.squeeze(switch)` and applies `tf.nn.dropout` — so a switch of `1.0` applies dropout at `rate`, and `0.0` passes the input through unchanged.

**`deepchem/models/keras_model.py`**:
- Added `import collections`.
- `_predict(...)` now takes an `outputs` argument. When provided, it fetches those specific Keras Tensors (via `session.run` in graph mode, or a temporary functional `tf.keras.Model` in eager mode) instead of the standard prediction outputs, and skips `_prediction_outputs` selection. A single tensor is wrapped into a list. Requesting `outputs` together with `uncertainty` raises `ValueError`.
